 Bank stocks hit record highs, but is the rally just getting started? Analysts cite tailwinds for more upside ahead
 SECTIONS Bank stocks hit record highs, but is the rally just getting started? Analysts cite tailwinds for more upside ahead By Debaroti Adhikary , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Nov 18, 2026, 11:18:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Bank Nifty has surged nearly 25% from its April lows to hit a record high above 62,440. Easing oil prices, a revival in FII inflows, strong credit growth and attractive valuations have lifted sentiment. Analysts remain positive on select large-cap private banks and see further opportunities across the sector.
 ETMarkets.com ​From war-led worries to renewed investor appetite, banks are finding fresh momentum on Dalal Street.
 Banking stocks have seen a sharp rally recently, pushing the Bank Nifty index to a lifetime high above 62,000. Even after such a sharp run-up, analysts remain optimistic, citing attractive valuations and further room for upside.
 Earlier this year, the Middle East war sent crude oil prices soaring and rattled global markets, putting banking stocks under pressure as analysts flagged risks to India's economy. In the first 100 days of the conflict, banking and financial services emerged among the worst-hit sectors, with the Nifty PSU Bank index plunging 16% and wiping out nearly Rs 4 lakh crore in market value.
Another major drag was the leadership worries at heavyweight HDFC Bank . The stock saw a sharp drop earlier this year, which was triggered after former part-time Chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned, stating that some practices within the bank did not match his personal values and ethics. The governance cloud led to a massive selloff that recovered slightly after the bank made leadership changes. Lacklustre first quarter earnings further dampened sentiment.
 Also read | HDFC Bank shares jump 22% from 52-week low in 10 days; analysts see private lender nearing an inflection point. Time to buy or wait? 
But as the war eased and oil prices dropped from the multi-year highs, analysts began pointing out attractive valuations, while strong earnings growth further boosted the rally. Additionally, HDFC Bank addressed the leadership worries, appointing a new CEO. Further, the sharp revival in FII inflows further fuelled the rally in banking stocks.
 Live Events
 As bank stocks rallied, so did Nifty Bank. After hitting a 52-week low of 49,955 in early April this year, the index surged nearly 12,500 points or 25% in a little over seven months to hit a lifetime high above 62,440 on Tuesday.
 Also read | Nifty Bank hits new record high as old warhorse HDFC Bank powers 13% November rally 
 Should you buy, sell or hold bank stocks now?
Strong systemic credit growth across segments, positive margins outlook underpinned by RBI rate hikes, sufficient liquidity aided by FCNR(B) deposit accretion and lower slippages resulting in benign asset quality are some of the reasons for the recent banking sector rally, according to Sunny Agrawal, Head of Fundamental Research at SBI Securities. He further added that the valuations had turned attractive over the past quarters amid a downbeat market environment, especially the largecap private sector banks, which have been driving the majority of gains in the recent Bank Nifty rally.
Going ahead, Agrawal from SBI Securities is constructive on largecap private banks like ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and HDFC Bank, as well as small and midcaps DCB Bank, Karur Vysya Bank and City Union Bank.
HDFC Bank still trades at an attractive valuation, while ICICI Bank will continue to command premium valuations, underpinned by a strong franchise, stable asset quality and best-in-class profitability metrics, according to Agrawal. “We are selective in the PSBs and prefer Indian Bank,” he said.
“Sector fundamentals remain robust, with healthy Q2 FY27 earnings, accelerated credit growth of around 19%, strong deposit mobilisation aided by FCNR inflows, and stable asset quality near multi-year lows. This combination of foreign buying, lower oil, and solid operating trends has enabled banks to outperform,” said Pranay Aggarwal, Director & CEO at Stoxkart.
